app/engines/audio_ops.py.purpose: Audio processing: WAV<->MP3, duration probing, stitching

exports.name: compute_peaks_sidecar
exports.contract: (wav_path: Path) -> dict|None. Versioned (SIDECAR_VERSION=2; PEAKS_PER_SEC=60, PEAKS_MAX=200_000 -- bumped from v1's 8/100k, loader treats a version mismatch as stale and recomputes) downsampled peaks sidecar: {version, peaks([0,1] max-abs/bucket), duration_sec, sample_rate, channels, peaks_per_sec, source:{filename,size_bytes,mtime_ns}}. Stats the WAV before+after computing; a mismatch (concurrent re-render) returns None rather than caching a torn read. 2026-07-10 review hardening: PEAKS_MAX_DECODE_SAMPLES=20_000_000 caps decoded INPUT sample count (ffmpeg -ar downsample when duration_sec*sample_rate would exceed it) -- previously only the OUTPUT bucket count (PEAKS_MAX) was capped, a real memory/CPU DoS-caliber gap for long WAVs inside a sync request handler.

exports.name: ensure_peaks_sidecar
exports.contract: (wav_path, sidecar_path=None) -> dict|None. Single-owner cache wrapper around compute_peaks_sidecar: reads a fresh cached sidecar if version+source stat match, else computes and atomically writes. Called from two paths sharing this one implementation: (1) proactively at chapter render finalization (orchestrator.py TaskOrchestrator._emit_chapter_peaks_sidecar), (2) lazily on first GET request (chapters_assets.py _load_or_compute_peaks_sidecar).

notes: finalize_sample_artifact keeps WAV if MP3 conversion fails
2026-07-11 waveform fixes: compute_peaks_sidecar density PEAKS_PER_SEC 8->60, PEAKS_MAX 100k->200k, SIDECAR_VERSION 1->2 (mismatch = stale, recompute). Max-abs-per-bucket aggregation unchanged.

2026-07-11/12: extracted ensure_peaks_sidecar as the single cache-format owner (_read_fresh_sidecar/_atomic_write_sidecar helpers); render-time emission hook added at orchestrator.py's one engine-agnostic completion point (scope=='chapter' synthesis only, best-effort/non-blocking, no backfill of existing chapters).

app/engines/system_resources.py.purpose: Best-effort host resource sampling (CPU/RAM/VRAM) for the Activity page's system-resource strip

exports.name: sample_resources
exports.contract: () -> ResourceSample {cpu_pct, ram_used_gb, ram_total_gb, vram_used_gb: float|None, vram_total_gb: float|None}. Never raises -- CPU/RAM via psutil (non-blocking cpu_percent), VRAM via a 2s-timeout nvidia-smi subprocess call that degrades to None on any failure (missing binary, timeout, non-zero exit, unparseable output).

notes: Pure, synchronous, no import-time side effects, no threads -- safe to call directly from a request handler (modular_architecture.md). No new pip dependency for VRAM (subprocess+nvidia-smi, not pynvml).
